F01_coverage: Coverage is complete only from 2000 to 2024, so that is the window we analyse
F02_world_trend: Each kWh is 11% cleaner than in 2000, but the world makes twice as many of them
F03_pca: Oil, gas and hydro span three-quarters of the variation between national electricity mixes
F04_embeddings: The grouping is visible before any colour is added, so the archetypes are not painted on
F04b_umap_stability: UMAP layouts change with seed and settings, but the same five groups stay together
F05_choose_k: k = 5 ties k = 4 on separation and stays stable; from k = 6 both scores fall
F06_profiles: Four archetypes lean on one source; the fifth spreads across nuclear, wind, solar and bioenergy
F07_weight: 61 oil-dependent systems make 0.4% of world electricity; 25 coal-heavy ones make half
F08_map: Archetypes follow geography: South American and African hydro, Gulf gas, Asian coal
F09_ci_by_archetype: Two tiers: hydro and diversified systems emit a quarter as much per kWh as fossil ones
F10_income: Income buys more electricity, not cleaner electricity
F11_effects: Archetypes differ in system size, continent and wealth, but not in import dependence
F12_surrogates: Four yes/no questions reproduce the five archetypes with 95% balanced accuracy on unseen systems
F13_transitions: Mixes are sticky: 149 of 208 power systems (72%) are in the same archetype as in 2000
F14_dumbbell: 14 of the 20 largest power systems got cleaner; Vietnam and Japan got markedly dirtier
F15_eu: Italy cut the carbon intensity of its power by 44% without leaving the gas archetype
